campbell.title: Campbell City Council — October 6, 2026
campbell.summary: The agenda for the October 6, 2026 Campbell City Council meeting listed items on how the city will handle legal services while it transitions to a new city attorney, and on pay and working conditions for certain city employees. It also listed a market adjustment to the city manager's salary.
keyTopics: Temporary legal services during the city attorney transition
Compensation and working conditions for unrepresented confidential, classified management and unclassified management employees
Market adjustment to the city manager's salary

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — October 21, 2026
saratoga.summary: The agenda for the October 21, 2026 Saratoga City Council meeting listed routine business such as approving past meeting minutes and bill payments, along with two property lot-split approvals. It also listed an annual update to city code rules and a proposal to start the process of creating a Climate Resilience District.
keyTopics: The agenda listed final approval of a two-lot parcel map for 14860 Farwell Ave.
The agenda listed final approval of a two-lot parcel map for 18510 Sobey Rd.
The agenda listed the 2026 annual code update, including a public hearing on changes to City Code provisions on scheduling appeals and qualifications for City Commissioners.
The agenda listed two resolutions: one to create a Climate Resilience District Task Force and one to begin the process of establishing a Climate Resilience District.
The agenda listed approval of minutes from the September 30 special meeting and October 7 meeting, plus acceptance of the 10/01 and 10/08 vendor payment check registers.

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — October 13, 2026
los-altos.summary: The agenda for the October 13, 2026 Los Altos City Council meeting listed routine business, including approval of minutes, financial reports, and several resolutions, along with a few discussion items. Items on the agenda included a new $78,000 residential electrification rebate program, updated Below Market Rate housing guidelines, and a review of the handbook for city commissions and committees.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a resolution to amend the FY2026-27 budget by appropriating $78,000 from the general fund for a residential electrification rebate program.
The agenda listed a resolution to approve Below Market Rate (BMR) for-sale and rental housing guidelines, with a finding that the action is exempt from CEQA.

The agenda listed resolutions to accept two completed public works projects: on-call sanitary sewer spot repairs and CCTV inspection services for FY 2025-2026, and the FY 2024-2025 Annual Streets Project constructed by O'Grady Paving, Inc.
The agenda listed a resolution to approve an updated Conflict of Interest Code for staff and commissioners under the Political Reform Act of 1974.

The agenda listed a discussion item to review the Commission and Committee Handbook and provide direction on revisions, plus an update on Ada's Cafe at the Community Center and the tentative Council calendar and Housing Element implementation schedule.

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 20, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026 Los Gatos Town Council meeting listed routine items such as approving minutes from two October 6 meetings and receiving August 2026 financial reports. It also listed several items asking the Town Council to authorize the Town Manager to sign contracts, including a first amendment with Foster and Foster, a three-year agreement, and an amendment to a lease.
keyTopics: Approval of the minutes from the October 6, 2026 Town Council Special Meeting and the October 6, 2026 Town Council Meeting
Receiving the August 2026 expenditure and revenue reports and the monthly financial and investment report for August 2026
Approving and ratifying the accounts payable check registers and payroll report
Authorizing the Town Manager to execute a first amendment with Foster and Foster
Authorizing the Town Manager or designee to enter into a three-year agreement, and to negotiate and execute an amendment to a lease

san-jose.title: San José City Council — October 20, 2026
san-jose.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026 San José City Council meeting listed routine business such as meeting minutes, excused absences, and special event approvals, along with several larger items. These included the City Manager's annual report, a police oversight report, planning priorities, and three land use items involving specific properties.
keyTopics: The agenda listed approval of a District 9 end-of-term farewell celebration and a District 5 Taiwan Retrocession Day proclamation and flag raising as Council-sponsored special events, allowing city funds and donated materials and services to be used.

The agenda listed retroactive approval of free use of the Janet Gray Hayes Rotunda for the Responsive Cities Network San José kickoff, and approval of District 9 SAP funds for the Rotary Club of San Jose Foundation.
The 2025-2026 City Manager's Annual Report and the 2025 Independent Police Auditor Year End Report were both listed for the Council.

The agenda listed a Citywide Planning Work Plan Prioritization item, along with early consideration of a privately initiated General Plan amendment for 525 Race Street and a conditional vacation of part of Spring Street between Asbury Street and West Taylor Street.
Two appeal hearings were listed: environmental and site development permit appeals for 470 West San Carlos Street, and an appeal of the in-fill exemption for a data center use at 300 Holger Way.

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — October 20, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026 Mountain View City Council meeting listed a 6:30 p.m. study session on interviews of applicants for the Environmental Planning Commission. The published notice also explained how residents can view meeting materials, submit comments by email or speaker card, request accessibility assistance, and challenge City decisions in court.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a 6:30 p.m. study session for Environmental Planning Commission applicant interviews.
Residents can email comments to city.council@mountainview.gov by 4:30 p.m. on the meeting date, with the agenda item number in the subject line, or fill out a blue speaker card to speak in person.
Agendas and reports are posted at mountainview.legistar.com and available at City Hall, the City Clerk's Office, and the Mountain View Library starting the Friday before the meeting.
The notice stated a 90-day deadline to challenge certain City decisions in Superior Court, and said court challenges may be limited to issues raised at the hearing or in writing beforehand.
Accessibility help is available by contacting the City Clerk at (650) 903-6399 or city.clerk@mountainview.gov 48 hours before the meeting.

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 6, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The agenda for the October 6, 2026 Sunnyvale City Council meeting listed recognitions for the Little League Junior Division All-Stars and several observances, followed by routine business items and a few larger proposals. Items before the Council included a ban on using drinking water to irrigate nonfunctional turf, a proposed Service Worker Retention Ordinance, and public art for the Lakewood Park renovation.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a public hearing and introduction of an ordinance to implement state law AB 1572 by prohibiting the use of potable (drinking) water to irrigate nonfunctional turf, amending the city's water conservation rules.
The agenda listed discussion and possible action to introduce a Service Worker Retention Ordinance.
The agenda listed approval of public art for the Lakewood Park renovation.

The agenda listed a proposal to raise the not-to-exceed amount of the WSP USA Inc. environmental consulting agreement for the SMaRT Station and Sunnyvale Landfill by $160,000, to $385,000, and extend it through October 17, 2028.
The agenda listed proclamations and recognitions for the Little League Junior Division All-Stars, Indigenous Peoples' Day, Friends of the Library Week, and Sunnyvale Stands United Against Hate Week.

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — October 20, 2026
cupertino.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026 Cupertino City Council meeting lists proclamations, a routine consent calendar with a bridge design contract and a gymnastics program contract, and two public hearings on health and safety planning and apartment financing. It also lists a discussion of how to lease a city-owned commercial property on Stevens Creek Boulevard. A special meeting and study session were noticed for 5:45 p.m., ahead of the regular 6:45 p.m. meeting.
keyTopics: The agenda listed recognitions for Domestic Violence Awareness Month, National First Responders Day (October 28), and United Against Hate Week (October 18-24).
The agenda listed a proposed approach for leasing the city-owned commercial property at 22100 Stevens Creek Boulevard.

The consent calendar listed accepting $850,000 in federal grant funds and awarding a design services agreement to Biggs Cardoza Associates, Inc. (up to $1,278,700) for the McClellan Road Bridge Project.

The consent calendar listed a contract with Red Line Gymnastics LLC (Bay Aerials Gymnastics) for gymnastics classes and camps, up to $480,000, with an option to extend two more years for a five-year total of up to $800,000.

Public hearings were listed on updates to the General Plan's Health and Safety chapter and related appendices (citywide), and on conduit financing for The RISE Block 5 Apartments Project, postponed from October 6.

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara Neighborhood-University Relations Committee — October 19, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The agenda listed a special meeting of Santa Clara's Neighborhood University Relations Committee for October 19, 2026, at 6:00 pm in the City Hall Cafeteria (East Wing, 1500 Warburton Avenue), with the option to join by Zoom or phone. The agenda listed routine items plus a discussion about neighborhood nuisance issues in rental leases in the Old Quad neighborhood. Residents could send written comments by email by noon the day of the meeting; those emails are added to the record but are not read aloud.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a discussion of neighborhood nuisance topics in private property leases, with possible direction to staff to return with ways to share the committee's input with property owners in the Old Quad neighborhood.
The agenda listed approval of the minutes from the committee's May 18, 2026 meeting.
The agenda listed the committee's 2027 meeting calendar.
The agenda listed updates from the Community Development Department, Santa Clara University, and the Police Department.
Public comment could be submitted to PlanningPublicComment@santaclaraca.gov by 12 p.m. on the meeting day, with the agenda item number in the subject line.

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — October 20, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council's October 20, 2026 agenda listed routine business such as meeting calendars and past minutes, along with items on park design work, a mosquito control presentation, renaming city community spaces, and annual reports and work plans for city commissions.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a resolution to rename the Cesar Chavez Community Garden to "Milpitas Community Garden," rename Cesar Chavez Plaza to "Milpitas Civic Center Plaza," and name the community garden in Delano Manongs Park the "Larry Itliong Community Garden."
The agenda listed an amendment to the design services agreement with Callander Associates Landscape Architecture for the Metro Tango Subdistrict Park Project, in an amount not to exceed $130,000.
The agenda listed a presentation from the Santa Clara County Mosquito and Vector Control District.

The agenda listed acceptance of the FY2025-26 Commission Annual Report and approval of FY2026-27 work plans for eight city commissions, including the Arts Commission, Economic Development and Trade Commission, and Library and Education Advisory Commission.

The agenda listed routine items: the October and November 2026 meeting calendar, minutes from the October 6, 2026 meeting, a preview of anticipated items for the next regular meeting, and the list of agenda items requested by Councilmembers.

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Architectural Review Board — October 15, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The agenda for the October 15, 2026 Architectural Review Board meeting listed a public hearing on AT&T's request to add new wireless antennas and equipment to two existing city-owned wood utility poles in the public right-of-way, near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue. The item is a quasi-judicial review, and the agenda notes the project is exempt from environmental review under CEQA as work on existing facilities.
keyTopics: AT&T's request (file 26PLN-00229) to review two wireless communication facilities on existing city-owned wood utility poles near 670 Guinda Street and 754 Homer Avenue
Proposed additions to the poles: new antennas, remote radio units, seven-foot fiberglass pole extensions, and associated equipment
Agenda lists the item as exempt from CEQA under the Existing Facilities exemption (Guideline Section 15301); the poles are in the public right-of-way, so no zoning district applies
A supplemental report was added to the agenda packet for this item
